campbell.title: Campbell City Council — July 7, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council considered a new interim ordinance related to state Senate legislation, along with public hearings on revoking the business license and tobacco retailer permits for two local shops, California Cigar and Hayes Smoke Shop. The council also considered authorizing a grant application for public works funding and approving consultant service agreements.
keyTopics: Interim ordinance implementing state Senate legislation, replacing a prior interim ordinance
Revocation of business license and tobacco retailer permit for California Cigar
Revocation of business license and tobacco retailer permit for Hayes Smoke Shop
Authorization for the Public Works Director to submit a One Bay Area Grant application
Approval of consultant service agreements

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — May 20, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council considered a resolution declaring the city's intent to identify properties designated for a special assessment or district program. The council also considered setting a public hearing for June 17, 2026, where residents could raise protests before the city finalizes its decision.
keyTopics: Resolution declaring intent to identify designated properties
Scheduling of June 17, 2026 public hearing
Process for residents to file protests
Steps toward final approval of the property designation

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — August 18, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council considered routine business including approval of prior meeting minutes, financial reports, and payment registers, along with a professional services agreement and an amendment to an existing contract. The Council also took up appointing a voting delegate for the League of California Cities Annual Conference, an omnibus ordinance making minor updates to the Town Code, and a request to either continue or hear a public hearing on appeals.
keyTopics: Approval of the August 4, 2026 Town Council meeting minutes
Monthly financial and investment report for June 2026
New professional services agreement and a second amendment to an existing agreement
Appointment of a voting delegate and alternate for the League of California Cities Annual Conference
Omnibus ordinance amending the Town Code and a decision on continuing or hearing a public hearing on appeals

san-jose.body: Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole
san-jose.title: San José Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole — August 19, 2026
san-jose.summary: The Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole met to plan upcoming City Council meetings, reviewing the finalized agenda for August 25, 2026 and the draft agenda for September 1, 2026. The committee considered adding new items to both agendas, deciding whether any items needed a scheduled 'time certain' for discussion, and reviewing any requests to waive standard notice requirements. The committee also took up the City Clerk's public record covering August 6 through August 13, 2026.
keyTopics: Finalizing the August 25, 2026 City Council agenda
Drafting the September 1, 2026 City Council agenda
Considering 'time certain' scheduling for specific agenda items
Reviewing waiver requests for agenda notice requirements
City Clerk's public record for August 6-13, 2026

mountain-view.title: Mountain View Youth Advisory Committee — August 17, 2026
mountain-view.summary: Mountain View's Youth Advisory Committee met to hear public comments, discuss plans for the city's Summer Movie Nights, and review the committee's overall role before electing members to leadership positions. Members also gave updates and shared comments on other city boards and committees they follow.
keyTopics: Public comments to the committee
Planning and updates for Summer Movie Nights
Discussion of the Youth Advisory Committee's purpose and responsibilities
Election of committee leadership roles (such as chair/vice chair)
Reports and updates from other city boards, commissions, and committees

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — August 11, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The Sunnyvale City Council held a special study session to consider raising the requirements for affordable housing in new residential developments and updating the fees that developers can pay instead of building those affordable units. The regular 7 P.M. Council meeting followed, opening with the Salute to the Flag.
keyTopics: Proposal to increase inclusionary housing requirements for new rental and ownership housing developments
Updating below market rate (BMR) in-lieu fees developers pay instead of building affordable units
Council Priority Project CDD 23-01 on affordable housing policy
Study session format allowing focused discussion before the regular Council meeting

cupertino.title: Cupertino Teen Commission — August 12, 2026
cupertino.summary: Cupertino's Teen Commission met to plan the upcoming Bike Fest event and discussed the Juvenile Traffic Diversion Program, which offers young people alternatives to standard traffic citations. The commission also heard from a youth-led organization called Next Vision AI and approved minutes from its June meeting.
keyTopics: Planning for the Bike Fest event
Juvenile Traffic Diversion Program overview
Presentation from youth-led group Next Vision AI
Approval of June 10, 2026 meeting minutes
Public comment period for non-agenda items

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — August 18, 2026
santa-clara.summary: This Santa Clara City Council meeting notice covered mainly logistical details: Councilmember Chahal participated remotely from India, and the meeting was held in a hybrid format with both in-person attendance and options for residents to join or comment via Zoom or phone. No specific policy items were detailed in the agenda excerpt provided.
keyTopics: Councilmember Chahal's remote participation from Panchkula, India
Hybrid meeting format combining in-person and remote access
Zoom and phone call-in details for public participation
Instructions for submitting written public comments before the meeting

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — August 3, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council considered a resolution to place a Business Tax Modernization Measure on the ballot, which would shift the city's business tax from a flat fee to a tiered gross receipts system based on how much revenue a business actually generates. City staff presented the proposal as a way to make the tax fairer, protect small businesses, and keep Milpitas competitive with other cities while updating the system for today's economy.
keyTopics: Proposal to replace Milpitas' current business tax with a gross receipts-based tax
Impact on small businesses, with about 85% of local businesses expected to see limited or no increase
Comparison of projected revenue per resident and per business against other cities
Simplifying tax administration through a tiered rate structure
Placing the business tax measure before voters

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Architectural Review Board — August 6, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Architectural Review Board considered staff recommendations on process and design standards for Tier 2 and Tier 3 wireless communication facilities located in the public right-of-way, such as antennas and equipment mounted on poles along streets. This item was determined not to be a project under CEQA, meaning it falls outside that environmental review process entirely.
keyTopics: Design standards for wireless equipment installed on public streets and sidewalks
Differences in review requirements between Tier 2 and Tier 3 facility classifications
Staff presentation outlining proposed processes for approving right-of-way wireless installations
How new standards could affect the look and placement of poles and antennas citywide
